About the School

Advancing
Agriculture
& Sustainability.

The School of Agriculture is an ICAR-Accredited institution, dedicated to shaping the next generation of agtech pioneers, researchers, and agribusiness entrepreneurs. Our industry-aligned curriculum integrates core scientific principles with advanced modern technologies—including precision farming, remote sensing applications, and smart irrigation systems—to address the global challenge of sustainable food security.

ICAR-Aligned Curriculum: Academic tracks at the Undergraduate (B.Sc. Hons.), Postgraduate (M.Sc.), and Doctoral (Ph.D.) levels are strictly designed around modern regulatory benchmarks, ensuring high global employability and research relevance.

Advanced Research Infrastructure: Students move beyond the classroom to train in state-of-the-art facilities, including the region's pioneering Hydroponics Working Laboratory, specialized Soil Science testing setups, and advanced Plant Pathology units.

Experiential & Field-Based Learning: Through our dedicated instructional farms and protected cultivation polyhouses, theory translates directly into practice. Students master everything from crop production management to advanced Integrated Pest Management (IPM) strategies.

Entrepreneurship & Global Networks: We foster a robust ecosystem for student innovation, preparing graduates for high-impact roles in agribusiness management, agro-pharmaceutical sectors, government research bodies, or independent agritech startups.

Message from

Dean - SCHOOL Of AGRICULTURE

//

Welcome to the School of Agriculture.
“A place where we don’t just study agriculture; we live it.”
Our mission is to bridge the gap between foundational agricultural wisdom and the frontier of modern agritech. In an era defined by shifting climates and evolving global food demands, agricultural education must move faster than the challenges it faces. We achieve this by embedding precision farming, sustainable resource management, and advanced biotechnological tools directly into our academic fabric.
Through rigorous hands-on field validation at our instructional farms, experiential learning in our pioneering Hydroponics Working Laboratory, and specialized research across our core Soil Science and crop protection facilities, we ensure our students graduate as industry-ready professionals. Whether your goal is to lead groundbreaking academic research, drive policy in environmental sustainability, or launch the next big agritech venture, we provide the ecosystem to make it happen. Join us to cultivate a smarter, greener, and more resilient future." //

Dr. (Prof.) Ajeet Singh Sekhawat

SCHOOL OF AGRICULTURE

Our Vision

  • Academic Excellence: To build a premier, nationally recognized center of excellence that sets the benchmark for high-caliber agricultural education and research.
  • Future-Ready Leadership: To cultivate highly skilled, tech-savvy professionals and innovative leaders prepared to navigate and drive the modern agribusiness sector.
  • Global Food Security: To pioneer advanced agtech solutions, precision farming methods, and climate-resilient field practices that safeguard global food supplies.
  • Rural Prosperity: To translate scientific innovation into real-world impact, driving economic stability, sustainable growth, and upliftment within rural farming communities.

Our Mission

  • Academic Excellence: To deliver high-caliber education across agronomy, horticulture, soil science, and allied disciplines, anchoring theoretical frameworks in modern scientific methodologies.
  • Targeted Research: To pioneer high-impact research in crop diversification, precision farming, biotechnological applications, and adaptive strategies for climate-resilient agriculture.
  • Experiential Learning: To solidify practical competencies through intensive field-based validation, advanced laboratory training, and direct exposure to modern agricultural mechanization.
  • Ecosystem Integration: To cement strategic alliances with agricultural industries, KVKs, ICAR institutions, and progressive farming communities for robust internships and collaborative research.

Have Questions?

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about the admissions, academics, and campus life at our School of Agriculture.

Still have questions?

Can't find the answer you're looking for? Please chat to our friendly team.

admissions@mygyanvihar.com Contact Us
Are classes taught by professors or teaching assistants?
All courses at the School of Agriculture are delivered exclusively by experienced Professors and Assistant Professors using multimedia teaching tools, modern projectors, and high-definition smart boards.
What is the average class size and delivery structure?
Student cohorts are maintained in Sections A, B, and C with an optimal strength of 30–35 students per class. Faculty members conduct dedicated Q&A discussions after lectures and structured revision sessions after syllabus completion.
What academic support and mentoring systems are available?
The School operates a dedicated Proctorial System where each student is assigned a faculty mentor at a 1:10 ratio. Weekly mentoring sessions support academic progress, field learning, and student well-being.
What is the academic workload outside lectures?
Practical learning is intensive, with mandatory laboratory and field sessions alongside theory classes. Advanced students also complete Experiential Learning Programmes (ELP) involving multi-disciplinary field operations.
What are the eligibility and entrance criteria?
Undergraduate admission requires 10+2 with PCM/PCB or Agriculture through JET or ICAR channels. M.Sc. admission requires B.Sc. Agriculture through SGVUEE, while Ph.D. admissions are conducted through the university research entrance framework.
Does the School have farms and field laboratories?
Yes. The department manages instructional farms, climate-controlled polyhouses, and advanced field laboratories for practical training in agronomy, horticulture, and soil testing.
Are internships and corporate field training available?
Yes. Students complete continuous field exposure and mandatory RAWE programmes, along with industrial attachments and agribusiness internships.
Does the university provide placement and competitive exam support?
Yes. The School coordinates with the Training & Placement Office for placement assistance and provides guidance for ICAR-JRF/SRF, NET, NABARD, IBPS AFO, and other competitive examinations.
